title: Exponential Taylor series convergence and Euler-number bounds

problemStatement.formal: For every real x, prove Summable (fun n => x^n/n!) and Real.exp x = sum' n, x^n/n!, derive partial-sum and remainder convergence, and prove the explicit Euler-number tail bound |e - sum_{k<n} 1/k!| <= 3/n! for n>=1.
problemStatement.plain: Backfill the exp-series metadata around the Lean proof: summability, tsum and HasSum forms, partial-sum convergence, Lagrange remainder, Euler-number series, the 3/n! approximation bound, and simple consequences such as e>2.
whyMatters: Taylor series convergence is a central analysis example with a clean Lean bridge to Mathlib's exponential series.
The explicit Euler-number tail estimate gives a concrete error bound, not just abstract convergence.
The file is a fully verified analysis slice with zero axioms and zero sorries.

proven: `exp_series_summable`, `exp_tsum`, `exp_hasSum`, `exp_partial_sum_tendsto`, and `exp_remainder_tendsto_zero` establish the exponential power-series interface.
`iteratedDeriv_exp` and `exp_lagrange_remainder` connect the proof to Taylor's theorem and Lagrange remainder form.
`euler_number_series`, `euler_tsum`, `euler_partial_sum_tendsto`, and `euler_approx_error` prove the Euler-number series and the explicit 3/n! tail bound.
`exp_infinite_radius`, `exp_one_gt_two`, and `exp_five_term` record radius and numerical consequences.
open: `TaylorTheoremOQ03.lean` has zero active axioms and zero sorries.
The file focuses on the exponential series; broader Taylor-theorem automation and other functions remain outside this slice.
knownResults.goal: Surface the verified exp-series and Euler-number error-bound anchors for gallery/search metadata.
